# Erdős Problem 29

open Filter Asymptotics AdditiveCombinatorics

namespace Erdos29

/--
Is there an explicit construction of a set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that $A+A=\mathbb{N}$ but
$1_A\ast 1_A(n)=o(n^\epsilon)$ for every $\epsilon>0$?

The existence of such a set was asked by Sidon to Erdős in 1932. Erdős (eventually) proved the
existence of such a set using probabilistic methods. This problem asks for a constructive
solution. An explicit construction was given by Jain, Pham, Sawhney, and Zakharov [JPSZ24].

The formal statement records the existence of such a set; the linked formal proof exhibits an
explicit construction.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos29.lean#L104"]
theorem erdos_29 : answer(True) ↔ ∃ A : Set ℕ, A + A = Set.univ ∧ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
    (fun n : ℕ => (sumRep A n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ ε := by
  sorry

end Erdos29

reformulations.difference: Relative to the asymptotic-basis formulation in Er89d, p. 181, Lean requires A + A to contain every natural number, rather than every sufficiently large one. JPSZ24 already uses Lean's exact-coverage formulation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: If A covers every n ≥ N, adjoin F = {0,…,N}. Then B = A ∪ F covers all natural numbers. At each n, any representation added by this enlargement has at least one coordinate in F, so r_B(n) ≤ r_A(n) + 2|F|. A constant is o(n^ε) for every ε > 0, so the required growth condition survives. Conversely, exact coverage implies eventual coverage. A positive-integer convention can also be accommodated by translation, which preserves these asymptotics.

review.notes:
No mathematical defect found. The quantifier order selects one set working for every positive real exponent. `sumRep` counts finite ordered representations exactly as in JPSZ24. Scratch proofs establish equivalence with the source's quotient-limit condition and check the zero boundary, empty set, small finite sets, and the full set of naturals.

Explicitness is documented as a requirement on the exhibited construction rather than a complexity predicate in the theorem. The pinned proof genuinely defines an explicit mixed-radix basis using bounded searches. Its complete dependency tree compiled unchanged, and /workspace/review/proof_bridge.lean derives the exact reviewed proposition from that named witness without importing the sorry-backed problem theorem. Both proofs depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. This supports the affirmative answer, solved status and formal_proof record; no formal running-time bound is asserted by the reviewed declaration.

Access limitations: erdosproblems.com returned Cloudflare challenges despite descriptive User-Agent headers, and the relevant pages of Er97c were not accessible beyond its preview. The other primary references and the complete linked formal proof suffice to verify the declaration.
